problem: Generative visual-navigation policies (NoMaD, FlowNav, NaviDiffusor) output trajectories in a normalized, unscaled space, so deployment relies on a hand-tuned scale (v_max/f). They also execute only a single waypoint via a velocity controller, which cuts corners and collides with obstacles that the full path would avoid.
motivation: Without metric grounding, the predicted path cannot be safely executed in full or checked for collisions, and the tuned scale is neither metric nor robot/environment independent. Predicting the true inter-waypoint distance lets the full trajectory be executed and enables metric collision and goal guidance.
key_idea: Train ScaleNet to predict the metric average waypoint distance from the image, the depth tokens and the unscaled trajectory, so that generative-policy outputs can be executed as metric paths with a position controller and guided by a metric TSDF.
insight: Learning the scale beats the fixed v_max/f scale for all base policies. Executing the whole scaled path (position control) beats single-waypoint velocity control in both simulation and on the real robot. The MetricNav guidance mainly helps when velocity control is used (0.51 vs 0.45-0.46) and is only comparable under position control (0.61), so most of the gain comes from metric scaling plus full-path execution.
method: ScaleNet: predicts the scalar phi_pred that maps the normalized trajectory to metric scale. It encodes the trajectory with a 1D conv, image patches with EfficientNet-B0, and depth tokens from the frozen Depth-Anything-V2 ViT-S DINOv2 encoder plus a residual block. A transformer (6 heads, 3 layers) over a CLS token and these tokens feeds an MLP; trained with MSE against phi_gt, the mean waypoint distance, with the loss scaled to mm.

Position control: with the metric waypoints, the robot executes the whole path from 0 to T_W (T_A=8, T_W=3) instead of steering toward one waypoint, then replans. On the real robot this is a rotate-then-translate strategy.

Collision cost: Depth-Anything-V2 ViT-B metric depth becomes a pointcloud, RANSAC ground removal follows, and a local TSDF that is non-zero in both free and obstacle space is built. The cost sums TSDF values at each waypoint and at the left/right robot boundary points.

Goal cost: K trajectories are sampled and spherical k-means on the N-th waypoint direction selects the most likely goal direction. The cost is 1 minus the cosine similarity between each action's N-th waypoint and that direction.
Guided denoising: gradients of alpha*F_goal + beta*F_coll (alpha=0.5, beta=0.01, mu=0.1) are added to the denoising steps only for k<2.
Final action selection: each guided trajectory is scored by gamma*cosine goal similarity + (1-gamma)*negative collision cost, and the best one is executed.

Benchmark: a simulation benchmark in Habitat with 20 topological maps and 20 environments, tight curves, 5 seeds and TurtleBot4 collision checking, measuring topomap fraction reached (navigation) and distance before collision (exploration).

setting.backbone: ScaleNet (EfficientNet-B0 + frozen Depth-Anything-V2 ViT-S + small transformer, trained) on top of NoMaD/FlowNav/NaviDiffusor diffusion/flow policies; Depth-Anything-V2 ViT-B for metric depth
setting.training_data: ScaleNet: about 1.5M data points from GoStanford, RECON, Tartan Drive, SACSoN, SCAND plus 16k Habitat trajectories over 800 Matterport3D scenes. Baseline policies are retrained on the same split, with synthetic data for benchmarking and real data for deployment.
setting.observation: monocular RGB (fisheye, 15 Hz) with an observation context of 4 frames, plus a goal image; depth is estimated from RGB
setting.action_space: predicted 2D waypoints (8 horizon) executed by a velocity controller or a position controller (rotate-translate)

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 topological maps in 20 environments, 5 seeds (2k repetitions per baseline)
numbers.extra: synthetic-trained policies; velocity control with T_W=1
numbers.evidence: Table II: Average fraction of the topomap completed, Vel. control, MetricNav 0.51
Table I: MetricNav (ours) position control 0.96 SR, 0.6 #Coll

numbers_note: Simulation exploration results (distance before collision) are given only as box plots in a figure. The paper prints SR as fractions 0-1.
results: ScaleNet with position control improves all baselines over the fixed-scale velocity control. In simulation NoMaD/FlowNav/NaviDiffusor reach 0.59/0.61/0.61 with position control vs 0.46/0.45/0.46 with velocity control. On the real robot MetricNav reaches SR 0.96 with 0.6 collisions per run, vs NaviDiffusor 0.93 (0.8 collisions) with position control.
limitations: MetricNav gives no gain over the baselines under position control in simulation (0.61 vs 0.61), and the real-world test is a single ~20 m corridor with 5 runs.
The controller is not reactive to dynamic obstacles, and the guidance is slower on a laptop GPU, so it is less suited to velocity control.
Depends on approximate camera intrinsics and monocular metric depth for the TSDF; the benchmark is custom, with no standard benchmark comparison.
